previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain, fever, and cloudy urine, two weeks after a prior hospitalization for pyelonephritis. He has a history of neurogenic bladder with a urostomy and a left nephrostomy tube due to ureteral stricture and severe hydronephrosis. He was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis caused by Escherichia coli, with acute kidney injury on stage IV CKD and hyponatremia. He was started on empiric IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line. His infection resolved, renal function improved, and electrolytes stabilized. He was discharged home with home health services to complete a three-week course of IV antibiotics, with follow-up planned in urology, nephrology, and primary care, including nephrostomy tube management and monitoring of a lung nodule.

Foot bx wound ___:
Skin, left foot overlying MTP joint, biopsy:
- Superficial ulcer with adjacent irregular epidermal 
hyperplasia and subadjacent granulation tissue
with scattered eosinophils (see note).
Note: No bacteria, fungi, or acid fast bacilli are seen on 
Brown-Brenn, PAS, and ___ stains. No
vascular calcifications are seen in this sample (depth limited 
to dermis, ___ stain examined).
The ulcer bed contains degenerated collagen, fibrin, and 
cellular debris, features along with the
adjacent reactive epidermal hyperplasia and granulation tissue 
suggest a traumatic/irritation etiology.
Correlation with tissue culture is, however, needed to 
definitively exclude infection. The presence of
eosinophils, while scattered, raises the possibility of a 
superimposed reaction to a contactant. 
 
 

 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o male with a PMH of T12 paraplegia secondary to MVA 
complicated by neurogenic bladder s/p ileal conduit/ileostomy 
(___) with refluxing R ureter and L ureteral structure 
requiring percutaneous nephrostomy with recurrent urinary tract 
infections as well as stage IV bilateral greater trochanter and 
ischial ulcers requiring repeated surgical debridements and flap 
procedures admitted to ___ with fever, fatigue, and open 
ulcers.
    
# Sacral and R Hip Pressure Ulcers:
Pt presented with superinfected ulcer, with foul smelling, 
purulent drainage on admission and significantly elevated 
inflammatory markers. The wound care team and plastic surgery 
teams were consulted.  Pt underwent several bedside debridement 
of necrotic tissue (no cultures were sent as plastics team felt 
necrotic tissue would be polymicrobial).  ID was consulted and 
pt was started on daptomycin and meropenem.  MRI was recommended 
to evaluate for OM but patient declined. Plastics confident 
wound did not extend to sacral bone and not representing 
osteomyelitis. Blood cultures were obtained and were negative.  
Upon discharge patient completed a 2 week course of Daptomycin 
and Meropenem (___) and will f/u with ID as an 
outpatient. He will also f/u with plastic surgery Dr ___ to 
monitor healing of his wounds.
      
# L Foot Traumatic Ulcer: 
Super infected, treated with abx as above.  The wound was 
treated per wound care when the patient permitted.
   
# Possible UTI: 
Noted on ___ to have klebsiella/e. coli in UCx. Patient 
chronically colonized, but also hx of multiple UTIs in the past. 
 Likely the this fevers on presentation were more likely ___ 
infected wounds rather than UTI. He was treated with abx as 
outlined above.
   
# Hyperkalemia:
Pt developed K to 5.7 on ___. He declined tx with medications, 
IVF or telemetry.  He preferred to drink water only and would 
avoid juices which were at his bedside. Repeat K ___ was 
normal.
  
# Chronic Pain: continued home meds
# Depression/Anxiety: continued home meds
# CKD Stage: GFR 22. Cr at baseline at 3.0

dislodged on ___. ___ consulted and recommended KUB which pt 
declined. Pt agreed to have stat lock placed.
